records.subject: Request for Revision and Enhancement of SDRF/NDRF Norms of Assistance in view of rising costs and increasing disaster-related losses.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Jogen Mohan:

I seek to raise the need for comprehensive revision and enhancement of the norms of assistance under the SDRF (State Disaster Response Fund) and NDRF (National Disaster Response Fund). The existing norms, notified vide No. 33-03/2020-NDM-I dated 11 July 2023, are based on 2022?23 levels and have become inadequate due to substantial increases in construction costs, labour, livestock, agricultural inputs and transportation. I urge the Government to undertake the pending mid-term review and suitably enhance assistance for damaged houses, public infrastructure, livestock, poultry, boats, handloom and textile losses, besides introducing appropriate provisions for restoration of educational institutions. I further request that, particularly for Assam and other flood-prone States, flood-control and anti-erosion works be brought within an appropriate SDRF/NDRF framework. I, therefore, urge the Government to expedite a comprehensive revision of the norms and periodically index assistance to prevailing market costs and inflation.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Request for granting UNESCO World Heritage Site status to Majuli, Assam.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Jogen Mohan:

I seek to bring to the notice of the Government the need for according UNESCO World Heritage Site status to Majuli in Assam, a globally significant cultural landscape and the spiritual and cultural heart of Assam. Majuli is the cradle of the Neo-Vaishnavite tradition founded by Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardeva and is renowned for its historic Satras, traditional performing arts, mask-making, manuscript preservation, music, dance and rich cultural traditions. Its unique heritage makes it an important representation of India?s civilizational and cultural diversity. Although Majuli has been included in India?s UNESCO Tentative List since 2004, it is yet to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The island is also facing serious threats from riverbank erosion, recurrent floods and climate-related challenges, which endanger its cultural heritage and traditional way of life. The recent inscription of the Charaideo Maidams as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024 has demonstrated the immense heritage value of Assam and the Northeast. It is, therefore, important to build upon this achievement and pursue the case of Majuli with urgency.

          I urge the Government to expedite the preparation and submission of the required nomination dossier and undertake necessary engagement with UNESCO for the inscription of Majuli as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Such recognition would strengthen the conservation of Majuli?s tangible and intangible heritage, promote sustainable tourism, create livelihood opportunities for local communities and enhance the global recognition of the cultural heritage of Assam and Northeast India.

 (ENDS)
